title: Empirical directed task-transfer matrix
hypothesis: Useful KS/SI/ER transfer is directional or pair-selective, so one symmetric dense Omega cannot represent it.
outcome: weakened: raw ER-directed asymmetry was dominated by task-count-dependent optimizer exposure; KS residual unresolved and SI residual negative after step matching

title: Exposure-controlled gradient compatibility baseline

evaluation.er_protocol: ordinary split for diagnostic evidence only; no ER performance claim

hypothesis: At least one task pair has persistent shared-parameter gradient conflict, norm dominance, or phase-dependent compatibility that classical MTRL's learned Omega does not represent or mitigate.
outcome: confirmed norm-dominance branch: baseline ER shared-gradient norm ratios averaged 7.243 middle and 8.962 late, exceeding 3 in both phases for 5/5 seeds; MTRL ratios were 7.129 and 9.004 and did not consistently improve. Persistent pairwise conflict was rejected. Omega magnitude saturated in 5/5 seeds, with one ER-edge sign flip.
decision: CONFIRMED diagnostic; targeted literature search is next, with no mechanism promoted

title: Scale- and reliability-aware task relation literature gate
hypothesis: At least one published explicit Task Relation Learning method models unequal task scale or reliability, maps directly to F9, and is faithfully implementable for heterogeneous deep classification without category drift.
outcome: No reviewed method satisfied all gates: explicit relation models lacked direct heterogeneous deep gradient-scale control or required incompatible aligned regression assumptions; direct scale methods were loss weighting/optimization; the recent informative-relation method crossed the decomposition boundary.

closest_candidate.blocker: aligned Gaussian multi-output regression and no direct gradient-scale mechanism

direct_symptom_match.blocker: optimization/loss-weighting category with no explicit task relation

title: ER data-regime gradient-scale control

evaluation.primary_endpoint: seed-level phase summary of per-task shared-gradient norms (max/min ratio, ER-to-smallest ratio)
evaluation.er_protocol: ordinary split as context only; no ER performance claim, no LOSO required for this diagnostic

hypothesis: ER shared-gradient norm dominance is primarily a data-regime / gradient-estimate-noise effect: raising ER per-batch contribution to KS scale with exposure held fixed removes most of the imbalance.
competing_explanation: The dominance is task-intrinsic at this representation and persists under matched per-batch composition.
independent_variable: ER per-task training sampling weight 11.5 versus 1.0 control (training split only)
control: fresh matched plain wavCSE at the same commit and seed with the standard concatenated sampler

arms.A2: pre-registered reverse direction: reduce KS/SI training contribution to ER scale, launched only if A1 is ambiguous

falsification.support_H1: exposure check passes and A1 late max/min norm ratio < 3.0 while A0 >= 3.0
falsification.reject_H1: A1 middle and late ratios both >= 3.0

screening_result.interpretation: supports H1 direction at one seed; confirmation required

implementation.sampling: deterministic WeightedRandomSampler with replacement, num_samples=len(training_data), task membership from component index_pattern including subset-wrapped components

execution_failures.outcome: failed before first optimizer step because IEMOCAP component is Subset-wrapped; corrected by 0162224e63c1f77d3aaa7228bc2a13f3f2d85b14
